verdict.rationale: Apify gives developers indirect levers over when results come back. They can block until a run finishes with the convenience call (apify-docs-23), or be notified asynchronously via webhooks when a run finishes or fails (apify-docs-14, apify-docs-29). They can also bound completeness up front with input caps such as maxCrawlPages (apify-docs-15) and cap retrieved results with the limit parameter (apify-docs-28). However, the evidence never shows precise control over the return point, such as a wait timeout or reading partial results from a run still in progress. Missing for 10: documented wait-timeout control, incremental or partial result retrieval while a run is in progress, an explicit latency-vs-completeness configuration, and independent hands-on corroboration.
